chapters.summary: This chapter contains 39 verses and records the Lord’s warning to all people to hearken and prepare for coming judgments, with the rebellious exposed and cut off. It identifies the revelations as a preface to published commandments and grants disciples authority to proclaim and seal. It recounts calling Joseph Smith and others to establish the church, translate the Book of Mormon, and proclaim the gospel, with promises of forgiveness for repentance and fulfillment of the Lord’s word.

This chapter contains 3 verses and records a revelation that the priesthood is revealed by Elijah the prophet before the great and dreadful day of the Lord. It states Elijah plants in the hearts of the children the promises made to the fathers, turning children’s hearts to their fathers. It warns that otherwise the whole earth is utterly wasted at the Lord’s coming.

This chapter contains 20 verses and records the Lord’s declaration that God’s purposes cannot be frustrated and that human transgression causes loss of privileges. Joseph is reproved for fearing man, transgressing commandments, and delivering sacred translation materials to a wicked man. He is commanded to repent to remain called and retain his gift. The section states the work will continue and explains the plates are preserved to bring knowledge of the Savior to various peoples, especially the Lamanites.

This chapter contains 7 verses and records a call to serve God in a forthcoming work, instructing servants to labor with full heart, might, mind, and strength to stand blameless. It states that desire to serve constitutes a call, compares the work to harvesting a ripe field, and lists qualifying attributes including faith, hope, charity, love, virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, brotherly kindness, godliness, humility, and diligence. It commands asking and knocking to receive and have doors opened.

This chapter contains 35 verses and records a revelation to Joseph Smith regarding Martin Harris’s request for a witness of the plates. The Lord affirms Joseph’s custody and covenant to show them only as commanded, and directs him to focus on translating. It promises three witnesses, warns of unbelief and coming judgments, commands Joseph to repent and keep commandments, sets conditions for Harris to receive a view, and instructs Joseph to pause translation if required for safety.

This chapter contains 37 verses and records a revelation to Oliver Cowdery about a coming work, harvesting souls, asking and receiving, and keeping commandments while seeking Zion. It instructs him to preach repentance, value wisdom over riches, and use a sacred gift discreetly. It affirms spiritual witness of the translation’s truth, commands support of Joseph Smith, offers a gift to translate, mentions hidden records, promises protection amid rejection, and commands faith, sobriety, and not to fear.

This chapter contains 8 verses and records the Lord’s words to John about his desire for power over death to remain and bring souls, promising John will tarry until the Lord comes and prophesy to many peoples. It contrasts John’s desire with Peter’s desire to come quickly to the Lord, affirms both desires, appoints John as a ministering angel to heirs of salvation, and grants keys of this ministry to John, Peter, and James.

This chapter contains 12 verses and records revelation to Oliver Cowdery promising knowledge through faith and an honest heart about ancient engravings and records. It explains revelation coming to mind and heart by the Holy Ghost, cites Moses leading Israel through the Red Sea, and identifies Cowdery’s gifts including the “gift of Aaron.” It commands keeping commandments, doubting not, asking in faith, not trifling, and seeking mysteries and ability to translate sacred hidden records.

This chapter contains 14 verses and records counsel to Oliver Cowdery to continue as scribe for Joseph Smith until the record is finished, with future opportunity to assist translating other records. It explains that Cowdery’s translating privilege is withdrawn for not continuing and for asking without studying. It instructs to study, then ask, with confirmation by a burning feeling or a stupor of thought. It commands patience, faithfulness, resisting temptation, and standing fast.

This chapter contains 70 verses and records a rebuke for losing translated writings and the gift, then restoration and commands to be faithful, not overwork, and pray. It warns of Satan’s plan to alter the lost manuscript and entrap Joseph if he retranslates. It instructs not to retranslate but to translate the plates of Nephi to King Benjamin. It states Christ’s doctrine: repent and come to him; his church is those who do so and endure.

This chapter contains 30 verses and records the Lord’s counsel to Hyrum Smith about assisting in a coming work and the cause of Zion. It commands repentance, obedience, seeking wisdom over riches, and trusting the Spirit. Hyrum is told not to preach until called, to study and obtain the word, keep peace, and be patient while translation proceeds. It affirms revelation and Jesus Christ’s identity and promises to believers power to become sons of God.

This chapter contains 9 verses and records the Lord announcing a coming work and urging attention to His word. It describes the field being ready for harvest and promises that those who desire to labor are called of God. It instructs seekers to ask and knock, to keep commandments, and to help establish Zion. It lists required qualities: humility, love, faith, hope, charity, and temperance.

This chapter contains 1 verse and records the conferral of the Aaronic Priesthood in the name of the Messiah, stating it holds keys for the ministering of angels, the gospel of repentance, and baptism by immersion for remission of sins, and declaring it will not be taken from the earth until the sons of Levi again offer an offering to the Lord in righteousness.

This chapter contains 11 verses and records the Lord declaring a great work coming forth and urging heed to His word. It calls willing laborers to harvest and promises salvation for enduring and keeping commandments. It commands seeking to establish Zion, asking in faith, and receiving the Holy Ghost to witness and declare repentance. Jesus Christ identifies Himself and states He will bring the fulness of the gospel from the Gentiles to Israel, calling David to assist.

This chapter contains 6 verses and records Jesus Christ addressing John, declaring His power and personal knowledge of John’s desires. It notes John’s desire to know what is most worth to him and blesses him for speaking Christ’s words by commandment. It instructs John that the most valuable work is to declare repentance to the people, bring souls to Christ, and rest with them in the Father’s kingdom.

This chapter contains 6 verses and records Jesus Christ addressing Peter Whitmer Jr., commanding him to hearken and noting divine authority over the earth. It states that Christ knows matters privately shared with Peter and acknowledges Peter’s repeated desire to know what is most valuable to him. Peter is blessed for speaking Christ’s words by commandment. Peter is told that his most valuable work is to declare repentance to the people to bring souls to Christ and rest with them in the Father’s kingdom.

This chapter contains 9 verses and records a command to rely on the Lord’s word and obtain, by faith, a view of the plates and related artifacts (breastplate, sword of Laban, Urim and Thummim, and Liahona). After seeing, the witnesses testify by God’s power to protect Joseph Smith and support the work. It affirms Joseph’s translation as true, promises grace and final exaltation, and declares Christ as speaker.

This chapter contains 47 verses and records revelation to Oliver Cowdery and David Whitmer affirming the truth of their writings and commanding reliance on what is written to found Christ’s church. It commands repentance, faith, hope, and charity; taking upon Christ’s name; and baptism with enduring to the end. It discusses the worth of souls, Christ’s suffering and resurrection, and calls for selecting Twelve disciples to preach, baptize, and ordain priests and teachers.

This chapter contains 41 verses and records Jesus Christ declaring His authority as Alpha and Omega, the final judgment, and the need for repentance to avoid suffering. It defines “eternal/endless punishment” as God’s punishment and recounts Christ’s suffering in Gethsemane. It commands repentance, confession, prayer, meekness, and preaching repentance and baptism. It forbids coveting and seeking life, directs supporting Book of Mormon printing, paying printer debts, imparting property, and preaching widely.

This chapter contains 84 verses and records the organization of the Church of Christ (6 April 1830), naming Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery as first and second elders, and recounting angelic ministry and translation of the Book of Mormon. It covers basic doctrines of creation, fall, atonement, repentance, baptism, and endurance. It gives requirements and wording for baptism and the sacrament prayers, outlines duties and authority of elders, priests, teachers, and deacons, sets conference and ordination procedures, and provides rules for membership records, discipline, children’s blessings, and letters of standing.

This chapter contains 12 verses and records a command to keep a record naming Joseph Smith as seer, translator, prophet, apostle, and elder, and dates the Church’s organization as April 6, 1830. It commands members to heed his words as from the Lord, promising protection. It mentions Zion, blessings on laborers, testimony of Christ’s crucifixion, and directs Oliver Cowdery to ordain him, appointing him first elder and preacher to Gentiles and Jews.

This chapter contains 4 verses and records the Lord declaring old covenants done away and establishing a new and everlasting covenant. It states repeated baptisms without proper covenant and authority avail nothing and that entry at the strait gate is not by the law of Moses or dead works. It explains this covenant and church are built up because of dead works. It commands entering as commanded and not counseling God.

This chapter contains 7 verses and records revelations to Oliver Cowdery, Hyrum Smith, Samuel Smith, Joseph Smith, and Joseph Knight. Oliver is warned against pride and told to declare his calling and preach truth. Hyrum, Samuel, and Joseph are called to exhortation and to strengthen the church, with Samuel not yet called to preach publicly. Joseph Knight is commanded to pray vocally and in secret, unite with the church, and exhort continually.

This chapter contains 19 verses and records counsel to Joseph Smith to repent, magnify his office, write and preach by the Comforter, travel to the churches in Colesville, Fayette, and Manchester for support, and endure afflictions. It directs Oliver Cowdery to proclaim the gospel. It restricts seeking miracles except as commanded, prescribes dusting feet against rejecters, promises protection from violence and lawsuits, and commands traveling without purse or scrip.

This chapter contains 16 verses and records a revelation addressed to Emma Smith, promising forgiveness and an inheritance in Zion if faithful. It instructs her not to murmur, to comfort Joseph Smith, act as his scribe when needed, and be ordained to expound scripture and exhort the Church. It directs her to lay aside worldly things, select sacred hymns, remain meek, avoid pride, keep covenants and commandments, and states the counsel applies to all.

This chapter contains 2 verses and records instructions to devote time to studying scriptures, preaching, confirming the church at Colesville, and required labor on the land until going west for the next conference, after which further duties are made known. It commands that church actions be done by common consent, with much prayer and faith, and that blessings are received by faith.

This chapter contains 18 verses and records Jesus Christ’s instructions on the sacrament, stating it matters not what is eaten or drunk if done in remembrance, and commanding not to purchase wine or strong drink from enemies but use what is made new among believers. It lists future communion with Moroni, Elias, John the Baptist, Elijah, patriarchs, Adam, and Peter, James, and John with priesthood keys. It commands taking the whole armor of God and being faithful.

This chapter contains 16 verses and records instructions to Oliver Cowdery: he may teach by the Comforter but only Joseph Smith receives commandments and revelations for the Church. Oliver is to support Joseph, avoid issuing commandments, and preach to the Lamanites, establishing the Church among them. It notes Zion’s location is unrevealed but near Lamanite borders. It directs conference order, correcting Hiram Page’s stone writings, and requires common consent.

This chapter contains 50 verses and records Jesus Christ forgiving the hearers, commanding them to sin no more, unite in prayer, proclaim the gospel, and gather the elect to one place to prepare for tribulation. It describes signs and judgments preceding Christ’s coming, resurrection, Millennium, final judgment, and a new heaven and earth. It covers creation by the Spirit, agency, Satan’s fall, Adam’s transgression, probation, redemption through repentance and faith, little children’s redemption, and commands the knowledgeable to repent.

This chapter contains 11 verses and records revelations to David Whitmer, Peter Whitmer Jr., and John Whitmer. David is reproved for fearing man, focusing on earthly things, and neglecting counsel; he is told to stay at his father’s house and continue ministry locally. Peter is commanded to travel with Oliver Cowdery, heed his counsel, pray, and assist his Lamanite mission under Joseph Smith. John is commanded to proclaim the gospel and labor near Philip Burroughs’ and in Zion without fear.

This chapter contains 13 verses and records counsel to Thomas B. Marsh: he is blessed for faith, promised blessings for his family, and called to preach what is revealed through Joseph Smith. He is told to labor in the harvest, with sins forgiven and temporal support promised, and to leave home briefly. He is promised receptive hearts and to help establish and strengthen a church, prepare for gathering, be patient, meek, and steadfast, serve as physician to the church, follow the Comforter, pray always, and remain faithful.

This chapter contains 5 verses and records instructions to Parley P. Pratt to declare the gospel, learn, and be meek. It appoints him to travel with Oliver Cowdery, Peter Whitmer Jr., and Ziba Peterson into the wilderness among the Lamanites, with the Lord promising to be with and advocate for them. It commands them to heed what is written, seek no other revelation, pray for understanding, and not trifle.

This chapter contains 18 verses and records the Lord’s counsel to Ezra and Northrop to preach the gospel at the “eleventh hour,” labor in a corrupted vineyard, and help gather the elect. It commands them to declare repentance, baptism by water, and the baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost, emphasizing faith in Christ. It references church establishment, articles and covenants, confirmation by laying on of hands, and use of the Book of Mormon and scriptures. It urges prayerful readiness for Christ’s coming.

This chapter contains 12 verses and records the Lord speaking to Orson, identifying Himself as Jesus Christ, the light and life of the world. Orson is blessed for believing and is called to preach the gospel, cry repentance, and prepare for the Lord’s second coming. It states Christ will come in a cloud with power and glory; nations tremble; signs include darkened sun, moon turned to blood, falling stars, and destruction of the wicked. Orson is told to prophesy by the Holy Ghost and promised divine presence if faithful.

This chapter contains 27 verses and records the Lord identifying Himself as Jesus Christ and addressing Sidney Rigdon, calling him to a greater work, commanding him to baptize and confer the Holy Ghost by laying on of hands, and promising signs to believers. It covers preaching the fulness of the gospel through Joseph Smith, keys and revelations, Sidney’s assignment to write for Joseph, exhortations to keep commandments, support Joseph, and promises concerning Zion, Israel, and the Lord’s coming.

This chapter contains 8 verses and records the Lord addressing Edward, forgiving his sins and calling him to preach the gospel. Sidney Rigdon is to lay hands on him so he receives the Holy Ghost. Edward is to declare “Hosanna.” Those who accept this calling before Sidney Rigdon and Joseph Smith are to be ordained and sent to preach repentance among nations. Elders may likewise be ordained. Christ commands preparation and says he will come to his temple.

This chapter contains 4 verses and records a command to pause translation work until going to Ohio due to the enemy. It directs members to preach the gospel locally and strengthen the church where found, especially in Colesville. It commands the church to assemble in Ohio in anticipation of Oliver Cowdery’s return. It instructs each person to choose for himself until the Lord comes.

This chapter contains 42 verses and records the Lord identifying Himself as Jesus Christ, warning of corruption, hidden plots, and coming judgment, and calling the Saints to prepare and be purified. It commands unity, mutual esteem, virtue, and teaching by appointed offices. It directs the gathering to Ohio to receive law and power, appoints men by church voice to manage property and aid the poor, warns against pride, and urges labor, meek warning, and separation from wickedness.

This chapter contains 24 verses and records Jesus Christ identifying himself and defining his gospel as repentance, water baptism, and baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost. It addresses James, calls him to be baptized, preach the fulness of the gospel, labor in the vineyard, build the Church, and help bring forth Zion. It directs him to go to Ohio, urges gathering there, calls for missionary labor and repentance, and commands baptism and laying on of hands for the Holy Ghost in preparation for Christ’s coming.

This chapter contains 3 verses and records a revelation about James Covel: his heart is right and he covenants to obey God’s word, receives it gladly, then is tempted by Satan and, fearing persecution and worldly cares, rejects the word. It states he breaks his covenant and God will deal with him as seems good.

This chapter contains 12 verses and records the Lord commanding the elders to assemble and, through faithful prayer, receive His law to govern the Church. It states Christ will come quickly and require obedience; those who claim to receive the law but do not follow it are not disciples and are cast out. It directs building a house for Joseph Smith to live and translate, permits Sidney Rigdon to live as he sees fit while keeping commandments, and calls Edward Partridge to be sustained and ordained bishop, leaving merchandise to labor for the Church.

This chapter contains 93 verses and records instructions to assembled elders to preach and baptize, travel west, and await revelation on New Jerusalem; affirms Edward Partridge’s office and requires authorized ordination. It gives commandments (no murder, theft, lying, adultery; marital fidelity; avoid evil speaking, pride, idleness), establishes consecration, stewardships, storehouse, and support for poor and leaders, outlines care and healing of the sick, and details church discipline and trials with witnesses and referral to civil law.

This chapter contains 35 verses and records instructions to church elders to accept commandments and revelations only through the appointed revelator (Joseph Smith), avoid deception, assemble to instruct and edify, purge iniquity, sanctify themselves, and provide for Joseph’s needs. It commands preaching repentance and preparing for the Lord’s coming, describes signs and judgments, the Millennium, Satan’s binding and release, and exhorts sobriety and keeping commandments.

This chapter contains 6 verses and records the Lord directing that the church elders be called together from all directions by letter or other means. He promises to pour out His Spirit on the faithful at their assembly. The elders are to preach repentance in surrounding regions, leading to conversions and power to organize under civil law for protection and preservation. They are commanded to visit and relieve the poor and needy.

This chapter contains 75 verses and records the Lord’s call to hearken to Christ as advocate, identifies Him as Alpha and Omega, and references the everlasting covenant. It covers prophecies of Jerusalem’s destruction and Israel’s scattering and gathering, wars, plagues, earthquakes, and heavenly signs preceding Christ’s coming. It describes resurrection, judgment on nations, Jews recognizing Christ, Satan bound, and the ten virgins parable. It commands translating the New Testament, gathering west, repenting, building churches, and establishing the New Jerusalem/Zion.

This chapter contains 33 verses and records instructions for church meetings to be conducted by the Holy Spirit, commanding members not to exclude people from public, sacrament, or confirmation meetings, with restrictions on partaking after trespass until reconciliation. It warns against deception and commands prayer and thanksgiving. It lists spiritual gifts (testimony of Christ, belief, administration, operations, wisdom, knowledge, healing, miracles, prophecy, discerning, tongues, interpretation) and assigns leaders to discern gifts.

This chapter contains 4 verses and records instruction that John is to write and keep a regular history, assist Joseph in transcribing revealed things until reassigned, and speak in meetings when expedient. John is appointed to keep the church record and history continually, while Oliver Cowdery is assigned to another office. The Comforter is said to enable John to write if he is faithful.

This chapter contains 6 verses and records instructions to remain temporarily in current residences. Those with land are to share with eastern brethren; those without land are to buy nearby homes for the present. Members are to save money and obtain means righteously to later purchase land for an inheritance and a city. The city’s location is not yet revealed; appointed men will receive it, purchase land, lay a foundation, and oversee gathering by family under church leaders.

This chapter contains 28 verses and records a commandment for Sidney Rigdon, Parley P. Pratt, and Leman Copley to preach to the Shakers, with Leman ordained to assist. It affirms Christ’s redemption, reign, and unknown return time; calls all to repent; and directs belief, repentance, baptism, and Holy Ghost by laying on of hands. It teaches marriage is ordained, forbidding marriage is wrong, and meats are provided with cautions against waste and bloodshed. It warns against deception about Christ’s coming and mentions end-time signs, Jacob, Lamanites, and Zion assembling.

This chapter contains 46 verses and records the Lord warning elders about false spirits, hypocrisy, and deception in the church. It instructs that preaching and receiving must be by the Spirit of truth, and that what does not edify is not of God. It teaches testing spirit manifestations by prayer in Jesus’s name and acting without railing. It promises increasing light, purification, and authority, calls Wakefield, Pratt, and Corrill to strengthen churches, corrects Partridge, and exhorts watchfulness.

This chapter contains 20 verses and records instructions to Edward Partridge to organize the Saints by divine law, appoint equal stewardships according to family needs, and give written inheritances subject to church worthiness. It sets rules for consecrated property, honest dealings, and not transferring assets to other churches without repayment. It directs appointing an agent and a storehouse under the bishop, provides for the bishop’s family, consecrates land temporarily, and promises reward to faithful stewards.

This chapter contains 44 verses and records instructions to elders to travel to Missouri for the next conference, with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon leading. It assigns multiple companionships to preach two by two, baptize, and lay on hands en route, and warns Lyman Wight. It gives a pattern to discern spirits, directs ordinations and reassignments, charges elders to support themselves, avoid idolatry, care for the poor and sick, and obtain church recommends.

This chapter contains 7 verses and records a revelation to Sidney Gilbert about his calling in the Church. The Lord says He has heard Gilbert’s prayers, commands him to forsake the world, and instructs him to receive ordination as an elder to preach faith, repentance, remission of sins, and the Holy Ghost by laying on of hands. Gilbert is also appointed to act as an agent for the Church under a bishop and to travel with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon, with further ordinances later.

This chapter contains 10 verses and records the Lord’s instruction to Newel Knight to stand fast in his appointed office. It calls brethren seeking to escape enemies to repent and be humble, and states a broken covenant is void, with warnings to offenders and mercy to covenant keepers. It commands the group to flee, choose a leader to manage funds, travel west to Missouri near the Lamanite borders, seek a living, and be patient in tribulation.

This chapter contains 6 verses and records a revelation to William W. Phelps: he is called, to be baptized for remission of sins and receive the Holy Spirit by laying on of hands, and to be ordained by Joseph Smith as an elder to preach repentance and baptism. It grants authority to confer the Holy Spirit on the contrite, assigns him to assist Oliver Cowdery with printing and preparing school books, and directs travel with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon, with Joseph Coe also accompanying.

This chapter contains 20 verses and records the Lord warning the rebellious and requiring disciples to take up the cross and keep commandments. It revokes and reassigns missions: Thomas B. Marsh travels to Missouri with Selah J. Griffin; Newel Knight remains with Saints in Thompson and leads contrite members who go. Ezra Thayre is commanded to repent, resolve land issues, or be cut off. The Lord rebukes sins, warns rich and unrighteous poor, and promises recompense, deliverance, and inheritance to the contrite poor.

This chapter contains 16 verses and records the Lord naming Missouri as the land of promise and Zion, identifying Independence as the center place and a temple site west of the courthouse. It commands saints to purchase surrounding lands. Sidney Gilbert is appointed agent to receive funds, buy land, and establish a store with licensed clerks. Edward Partridge is to divide inheritances. William W. Phelps is set as printer, assisted by Oliver Cowdery. Families are to be gathered and settled.

This chapter contains 65 verses and records instructions to church elders in Zion, promising blessings after tribulation and describing a future supper of the Lord for all nations. It appoints Edward Partridge as bishop and judge to divide inheritances, urges obedience to God and civil law, and teaches acting without being compelled. It directs Martin Harris and William W. Phelps to repent and manage consecrations, appoints an agent to raise funds, commands Sidney Rigdon to describe and dedicate Zion and the temple site, orders conferences, missionary preaching, orderly gathering, and disciplines Ziba Peterson.

This chapter contains 24 verses and records the Lord blessing those who come to Zion and obey the gospel, promising rest, inheritance, and rewards. It commands love of God and neighbor; prohibits theft, adultery, and killing; and requires gratitude and a broken heart. It instructs Sabbath observance, sacraments, prayer, confession, and proper fasting. It describes earth’s abundance for human use with judgment, not excess, and promises peace and eternal life for righteousness.

This chapter contains 17 verses and records the Lord’s instructions to elders returning from Zion, rebuking those who fearfully withhold preaching and warning their talents may be taken. It directs travel by craft to St. Louis, then appoints Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and Oliver Cowdery to go to Cincinnati and preach boldly. Others travel two by two preaching. Edward Partridge is to provide money. Commandments include not idling, not burying talents, returning while preaching, and shaking off dust in secret against rejecters.

This chapter contains 39 verses and records the Lord speaking to assembled elders, forgiving sins and warning of dangers and decreed destructions on the waters. Sidney Gilbert and William W. Phelps are told to travel in haste, while Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and Oliver Cowdery are commanded to avoid traveling by water except canals and to go by land. Instructions include forewarning others, preaching limits until Cincinnati, pairing missionaries, keeping Reynolds Cahoon and Samuel H. Smith together, and exhortations to watchfulness and prayer.

This chapter contains 9 verses and records the Lord speaking to elders, acknowledging human weakness and forgiving their sins for their testimony. He says their mission is not complete until they go to Zion, commands them to continue to Missouri, assemble, hold a meeting, rejoice, and offer the sacrament. They may return and preach together or in pairs, with faithfulness. He promises preservation, allows travel blessings if received gratefully, and directs them by the Spirit.

This chapter contains 66 verses and covers warnings against seeking signs, unbelief, and sexual sin; lists condemned behaviors; and promises inheritance to those who endure in faith. It commands saints to assemble to Zion without haste, purchase land, and send funds; predicts wars and coming judgment. It directs Titus Billings, Joseph Smith, and Newel K. Whitney in temporal arrangements and agency, with Oliver Cowdery assisting. It reproves Sidney Rigdon’s writing, urges repentance, proper use of the Lord’s name, prayer, and seeking a home by the Spirit.

This chapter contains 43 verses and records the Lord’s counsel to church elders to overcome the world, repent, and forgive all men, with directions for church discipline of the unrepentant. It names Joseph Smith and affirms keys with conditions of obedience, addresses sins of Ezra Booth, Isaac Morley, and Edward Partridge, and gives instructions about farms, business, and moving to Zion. It teaches sacrifice and tithing, warns of burning upon the wicked, outlines stewardship and judging in Zion, and foretells Zion’s flourishing and gathering.

This chapter contains 6 verses and records a proclamation to prepare the way of the Lord and make his paths straight. It states that keys of the kingdom of God are committed to man on earth and that the gospel will roll forth to all the earth. It instructs to prepare the supper of the Lamb and make ready for the Bridegroom, to pray and call upon God’s name, and to seek the kingdom’s spread in preparation for the Son of Man’s coming.

This chapter contains 13 verses and records a revelation to William E. McLellin: he is blessed for receiving the covenant but is told to repent of remaining faults. He is commanded to proclaim the gospel from city to city, not go to Zion yet, and not be preoccupied with property. He is sent to the eastern lands with Samuel H. Smith, to testify and reason in synagogues, heal the sick, be patient, avoid unrighteousness and adultery, and continue to the end.

This chapter contains 14 verses and records the Lord addressing assembled elders, acknowledging their prayers, noting fears that hindered blessings, and testifying of the truth of the commandments. It challenges them to produce a revelation like the least in the Book of Commandments and commands them to bear record if they cannot. It promises that if they humble themselves and abandon jealousy and fear, the veil will be rent and they will see and know the Lord by the Spirit, while teaching that natural man cannot abide God’s presence and counseling patience until perfected.

This chapter contains 35 verses and records a commission to Orson Hyde and other elders to preach worldwide, speak by the Holy Ghost, baptize, recognize signs, and seal converts. It outlines calling and rights of bishops, including descendants of Aaron, and trial procedures before the First Presidency. It commands parents in Zion to teach faith, repentance, prayer, Sabbath keeping, and baptize children at age eight; rebukes idleness and greed; directs Oliver Cowdery to deliver these sayings.

This chapter contains 8 verses and records the Lord directing John Whitmer to accompany Oliver Cowdery to Zion while Cowdery carries commandments and money. Whitmer is instructed to continue writing a history of important church matters and to receive counsel from Cowdery and others. Members abroad are told to send accounts of their stewardships to Zion, which is designated to receive these records. Whitmer is to travel among churches preaching, expounding, writing, copying, selecting, and gathering materials for the church and future generations in Zion.

This chapter contains 18 verses and records a commandment appointing Joseph Smith, Martin Harris, Oliver Cowdery, John Whitmer, Sidney Rigdon, and William W. Phelps as stewards over revelations and church concerns, accountable at judgment. It directs that surplus beyond needs goes to the Lord’s storehouse for Zion, requires equal temporal conditions without grudging, affirms laborers are worthy of hire in spiritual and temporal stewardships, and promises blessings, security, and inheritances for faithfulness.

This chapter contains 11 verses and records the Lord’s instruction to Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon to preach the gospel for a season, proclaiming from the scriptures with allotted Spirit and power. It directs them to labor in the vineyard, call people to repentance, and prepare for forthcoming commandments and revelations. It commands them to confront opponents publicly and privately, promises enemies will be confounded, and states no weapon formed against them will prosper while they keep commandments.

This chapter contains 26 verses and records instructions to assembled high priests to appoint a bishop and require stewards to render accounts. It appoints Newel K. Whitney as bishop in this part of the vineyard, directing him to keep the storehouse, receive funds, account for elders, and administer to needs, with debts handled through the bishop in Zion. It requires records, recommendations, and certificates for inheritance, Zion migration, and support of publishing revelations.

This chapter contains 6 verses and records the Lord directing elders to continue preaching and exhorting nearby churches until conference, where missions are assigned by conference voice. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon are instructed to resume translation and preach as practical until conference, then continue translation until finished. The instruction is set as a pattern for elders; they are told to gird up loins and be sober.

This chapter contains 7 verses and records an explanation that an unbelieving spouse is sanctified by a believing spouse and children are holy. It covers apostolic-era disputes over circumcision among Jews who reject the gospel, and how raising children under the law of Moses leads to adherence to tradition and unbelief. It cites Paul’s counsel against believers uniting with unbelievers to end circumcision and the tradition that children are unholy, affirming children are sanctified through Christ’s atonement.

This chapter contains 36 verses and records the Lord directing elders to preach without idling, promising blessings for faithfulness. William E. McLellin’s prior commission is revoked and reassigned south with Luke Johnson; other companions are sent east, west, and south. Missionaries are instructed to go house to house, bless receptive homes, and shake dust off against rejecters. The church is commanded to support missionaries’ families, ensure provision, reject idleness, and pair specific elders in ministry.

This chapter contains 119 verses and records a February 16, 1832 vision given to Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon while translating John 5. They testify of Jesus Christ at the Father’s right hand, Lucifer’s fall, and the fate of sons of perdition. It outlines resurrection and final judgment and describes celestial, terrestrial, and telestial glories, including the church of the Firstborn, spirits in prison, and varying inheritances and ministries.

This chapter contains 15 verses and records a question-and-answer explanation of symbols in Revelation. It defines the sea of glass as the sanctified earth; explains the four beasts, their eyes and wings, and the twenty-four elders; interprets the sealed book and seven seals as seven thousand years. It identifies four angels and an angel from the east sealing Israel, describes the 144,000, and addresses trumpets, a little book, timelines for events, and two end-times witnesses in Jerusalem.

This chapter contains 22 verses and records the Lord’s instruction to Joseph Smith and other high priests to organize an order to regulate the storehouse for the poor in Kirtland and Zion. It commands equality in temporal things, councils involving Joseph Smith, Newel K. Whitney, and Sidney Rigdon, and an everlasting covenant with penalties for breaking it. It promises the church’s independence, references Adam-ondi-Ahman and Michael, and emphasizes obedience, thankfulness, and faithful stewardship.

This chapter contains 4 verses and records the Lord’s will for Jared Carter to return to the eastern countries, traveling from place to place and city to city to proclaim the everlasting gospel by the power of his ordination. It promises the Comforter to teach him truth and guide his way. It promises a harvest of “sheaves” if he is faithful and commands him to be glad and not fear.

This chapter contains 5 verses and records a revelation directing Stephen Burnett to go into the world and preach the gospel to all who hear him. It appoints Eden Smith as his companion if desired. Burnett and his companion are instructed to preach in any direction without concern, to declare what they have heard and know to be true, and it states this is the will of Jesus Christ.

This chapter contains 7 verses and records a revelation to Frederick G. Williams to hearken to his calling as a high priest and counselor to Joseph Smith, who holds keys belonging to the Presidency of the High Priesthood. It commands faithfulness in counsel, continual prayer, and proclaiming the gospel. It instructs him to succor the weak and strengthen the feeble, promising a crown of immortality and eternal life if faithful.

This chapter contains 24 verses and records the Lord forgiving the saints as they forgive each other, warning against further sin and greater condemnation with greater light. It states the Lord is bound when commandments are kept. It commands Partridge, Whitney, Gilbert, Rigdon, Joseph Smith, Whitmer, Cowdery, Phelps, and Harris to form an unbreakable covenant order to manage bishopric affairs and care for the poor in Zion and Kirtland, holding properties equally for stewardship, enforcing church discipline for breaking the covenant, and urging leaving judgment to the Lord.

This chapter contains 6 verses and records the Lord’s instruction on church laws regarding women and children, especially widows and orphans. It states wives have claim on husbands for maintenance and remain in church fellowship if not transgressors; the unfaithful lose fellowship but may keep inheritances under civil law. Children have claim on parents until of age, then on the church storehouse if parents cannot provide inheritances. The storehouse is maintained by consecrations and provides for widows, orphans, and the poor.

This chapter contains 120 verses and records a revelation to Joseph Smith and elders about building New Jerusalem and a temple in Missouri, priesthood lineage and offices, and the greater and lesser priesthood. It states the oath and covenant of the priesthood, warns the church to repent and remember the Book of Mormon, and commands preaching, baptism, and avoiding boasting of signs. It gives missionary instructions, judgments on rejecting cities, consecration guidance, and assignments to Newel K. Whitney.

This chapter contains 12 verses and records the duty of the Lord’s clerk to keep Zion history and church records of consecrations, legal inheritances from the bishop, members’ lives, faith, works, and apostates. It directs that those not receiving inheritances by consecration have no names or genealogies enrolled. It foretells one “mighty and strong” to set in order the house of God and assign inheritances, and warns those not written in the books, including apostates, receive no inheritance.

This chapter contains 11 verses and records the Lord’s explanation of the parable of the wheat and tares: the world as the field, apostles as sowers, and Satan/Babylon sowing tares that drive the church into the wilderness. It instructs angels not to gather tares until harvest. It states priesthood continues through lineage, heirs are hidden with Christ, and must remain until the restoration of all things, urging faithfulness as a light to Gentiles and aid to Israel.

This chapter contains 8 verses and records a prophecy of wars beginning with the rebellion of South Carolina, leading to widespread conflict among nations. It states the Southern States divide against the Northern States and seek aid from Great Britain and other nations. It mentions slaves rising against masters and remnants vexing the Gentiles. It lists bloodshed, famine, plague, earthquakes, and heavenly signs, and commands saints to stand in holy places until the day of the Lord.

This chapter contains 141 verses and records the Lord’s instructions to assembled elders about the Holy Spirit of promise, the light of Christ, resurrection, and laws governing celestial, terrestrial, and telestial kingdoms. It describes earth’s sanctification and cosmic order, gives a parable of laborers, and commands prayer, sanctification, study, and organizing a school and house of God. It outlines end-time judgments, angels and trumpets, the Millennium, Michael’s battle, and rules for the School of the Prophets, including salutations and washing of feet.

This chapter contains 21 verses and records the Word of Wisdom given in Kirtland for the church, offered as a principle with promise. It warns against wine and strong drink (except sacramental pure wine), limits strong drink to washing, prohibits tobacco and hot drinks, and counsels use of herbs, fruits, grains, and sparing use of meat. It promises health, wisdom, strength, and protection from the destroying angel for obedient saints.

This chapter contains 37 verses and records the Lord forgiving Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and Frederick G. Williams, affirming their keys and presidency, and warning against treating revelations lightly. It commands organizing the School of the Prophets, finishing translation work, receiving revelations, setting churches in order, and studying languages. It gives housing and financial instructions, directs Vienna Jaques to go to Zion, and addresses repentance and chastening in Zion.

This chapter contains 6 verses and records the Lord’s counsel concerning the Apocrypha: it contains many true things and is mostly translated correctly, but also includes false interpolations by men. It states it is not needful to translate the Apocrypha. It instructs that readers should rely on the Spirit to manifest truth, and that those enlightened by the Spirit benefit, while those without the Spirit do not.

This chapter contains 2 verses and records a revelation commanding the united order, organized by prior commandment, to receive Frederick G. Williams into the order. It addresses Williams directly, instructing him to be an active member and promises blessings if he remains faithful in keeping former commandments, stating the instruction applies to all.

This chapter contains 53 verses and records the Lord’s promise that repentant, obedient souls see his face; Christ is the true light, one with the Father, creator, and grows grace for grace, as John testifies. It defines truth, light, intelligence, and agency; states spirits and elements are eternal and temples. It commands raising children in light and truth, rebukes Williams, Rigdon, Joseph Smith, and Whitney to set houses in order, urges prayer, preaching, scripture translation, and study for Zion.

This chapter contains 17 verses and records a commandment to lay out the stake of Zion in Kirtland beginning at the Lord’s house, following a revealed pattern. It designates two southern lots for buildings: a presidency house for revelations and ministry, and a printing house for publishing translated scriptures, each 55 by 65 feet with lower and higher courts, to be kept undefiled. It assigns inheritances to Hyrum Smith, Reynolds Cahoon, and Jared Carter, who serve as a building committee, and states the houses await further command.

This chapter contains 17 verses and records the Lord’s chastening and rebuke for neglecting the commandment to build His house, noting that many are called but few chosen and that contentions arose in the school of the prophets. It commands a solemn assembly and directs them to build a house where chosen servants may be endowed with power, to tarry, and to build not after the world. It specifies dimensions, appoints three to receive the pattern, and assigns lower and upper court uses.

This chapter contains 9 verses and records instructions to strengthen Zion by appointing Newel K. Whitney to take charge of a designated place for building a holy house and dividing it into lots by council for inheritances. It directs providing what is needed to benefit the order and publish God’s word. It accepts John Johnson’s offering, promises eternal life if obedient, and commands ordaining him into the order and removing encumbrances on the house.

This chapter contains 28 verses and records the Lord’s will concerning Zion, praising the humble and seeking. It approves a school in Zion and appoints Parley P. Pratt to preside, promising blessings and warning that unfruitful works face chastening. It commands building a house in Zion by tithing, for thanksgiving and ministerial instruction, requiring purity. It promises glory and prosperity if Zion obeys, and threatens judgments if she disobeys, while accepting her offering if she sins no more.

This chapter contains 48 verses and records the Lord’s comfort and promises to hear prayers, commands observance of constitutional law and support of wise leaders, and calls the Saints to forsake evil, renounce war, and proclaim peace. It reproves sins in Kirtland and warns of chastening. It gives instructions on bearing attacks patiently, conditions for warning and self-defense, rules for peace offers before battle, and requirements to forgive and bring testimonies before the Lord after repeated unrepented offenses.

This chapter contains 8 verses and records the Lord calling John Murdock to preach the everlasting gospel in eastern countries, traveling house to house amid persecution. It states that receiving Murdock is receiving the Lord, and he is given power to declare the word by the Holy Spirit. It outlines blessings for receivers, rejection and foot-cleansing testimony for rejecters, and coming judgment. It instructs him to delay travel until his children are provided for and sent to the bishop of Zion, with later inheritance in Zion optional.

This chapter contains 17 verses and records the Lord’s counsel to Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon that their families are safe, that many people are in the eastern land, and they should preach with meekness, speaking what is given them at the moment, with the Holy Ghost bearing record. Sidney is appointed spokesman to Joseph and empowered in scripture exposition. It mentions Zion’s future redemption, Orson Hyde and John Gould in the Lord’s hands, and promises salvation to obedient commandment keepers.

This chapter contains 101 verses and records the Lord’s explanation of the Saints’ afflictions and scattering because of transgression, with promised mercy, future gathering, and Zion’s eventual restoration. It describes conditions at the Lord’s coming and commands the churches to gather, stand in holy places, and buy lands around Jackson County. It gives parables on redeeming the vineyard and persistent petitions for legal redress, affirms constitutional principles and agency, and forbids Sidney Gilbert from selling the storehouse.

This chapter contains 34 verses and records the organization of the church high council at Joseph Smith Jr.’s house, naming Joseph Smith Jr., Sidney Rigdon, and Frederick G. Williams as presidents and twelve high priests as counselors. It sets quorum requirements, procedures to fill vacancies, and rules for hearing cases, evidence, speaking order by lot, voting, rehearings, and revelation on doctrine. It outlines councils abroad, reporting, appeals, and distinction from apostles’ decisions, and lists the lot results.

This chapter contains 40 verses and records a revelation on redeeming Zion and aiding scattered Saints, explaining chastening for disobedience and promising return if commandments are kept. It states Zion’s redemption comes by power and identifies Joseph Smith as the leader. It commands gathering to Zion, purchasing land with consecrated funds, and organizing companies (minimum 100; up to 500). It assigns roles to Sidney Rigdon, Parley P. Pratt, Lyman Wight, and travel companions.

This chapter contains 86 verses and records counsel on managing properties of the United Order, warning of curses for covenant breaking and authorizing discipline of unrepentant transgressors. It commands organizing stewardships and accountability, providing for the poor, and assigns specific stewardships in Kirtland to Sidney Rigdon, Martin Harris, Frederick G. Williams, Oliver Cowdery, John Johnson, Newel K. Whitney, and Joseph Smith. It separates Kirtland and Zion orders, establishes sacred and general treasuries, regulates common-consent withdrawals, and commands paying debts, seeking loans, and writing to New York.

This chapter contains 41 verses and records instructions about delaying Zion’s redemption due to the church’s disobedience, lack of unity, and failure to help the poor. It directs elders to wait, gain experience, and receive an endowment of power from on high in Kirtland. It gives counsel on remaining nearby or returning east by Joseph Smith’s appointment, maintaining humility and confidentiality, seeking legal redress, purchasing lands in Jackson County, and proclaiming peace.

This chapter contains 8 verses and records the appointment and ordination of Warren A. Cowdery as presiding high priest over the church in the land of Freedom, with instructions to preach, warn adjoining counties, and devote his full time to the calling with promised temporal support. It warns that the Lord’s coming is near and commands readiness. It notes heaven’s joy at Warren’s obedience, promises mercy, grace, assurance, and a crown if he remains faithful.

This chapter contains 100 verses and describes two priesthoods in the church (Melchizedek and Aaronic/Levitical), their names, keys, and associated offices. It defines quorums and authority of the First Presidency, Twelve Apostles, Seventy, and high councils, including unanimity and appeals. It gives priesthood lineage from Adam and events at Adam-ondi-Ahman, and outlines bishops’ roles, councils, and presidencies over deacons, teachers, priests, elders, and Seventy.

This chapter contains 8 verses and records a revelation to Lyman, forgiving his sins for obeying counsel, urging him to resist no more, and to be careful in keeping his vows. It instructs him to wait patiently for a solemn assembly, where he is to be remembered with the elders and receive ordination. It promises authority to preach wherever sent, commands him to strengthen the brethren, and assures divine help, blessing, and deliverance.

This chapter contains 80 verses and records a dedicatory prayer for the Kirtland temple. It thanks God for commanding the house and asks Him to accept, sanctify, and keep His presence there, excluding unclean things. It petitions for repentance, spiritual gifts, angelic protection, and power for missionaries, with outcomes for receptive or rejecting cities. It requests deliverance for Missouri exiles, mercy on nations and rulers, gathering of Israel, remembrance of Joseph Smith and church leaders, and final salvation and resurrection.

This chapter contains 16 verses and records visions in the temple where the Lord appears, declares his identity, forgives sins, accepts the house, and promises manifestations if commandments are kept and the house is not polluted. It then records Moses conferring keys for gathering Israel and leading the ten tribes, Elias conferring the dispensation of Abraham, and Elijah conferring sealing keys to turn hearts of fathers and children.

This chapter contains 11 verses and records the Lord addressing a journey to a city, stating He is not displeased despite follies. He says there is treasure and people there to be gathered for Zion, and directs forming acquaintances as led. He promises power to pay debts, mercy to Zion, and eventual influence in the city. They are told to tarry nearby, seek spiritual confirmation of where to stay, hire a place, inquire about founders, and act wisely without sin.

This chapter contains 34 verses and records the Lord’s counsel to Thomas B. Marsh, acknowledging his prayers, correcting him, forgiving his sins, and commanding him to preach to Gentiles and Jews and remain in Zion. It instructs the Twelve to be humble, admonish one another, follow Christ, and not rebel against Joseph Smith. Marsh is appointed to hold keys for missionary work among nations. It warns of coming wrath, commands worldwide preaching, baptism, and faithfulness, and affirms priesthood keys in the dispensation of fulness of times.

This chapter contains 10 verses and records questions and answers on Isaiah 11 and 52. It identifies the Stem of Jesse as Christ, the rod as a servant in Christ’s hands descended from Jesse and Ephraim, and the root of Jesse as a descendant holding priesthood and kingdom keys for gathering Israel. It explains Isaiah 52’s “put on thy strength” as priesthood authority in the last days and defines loosing neck bands as scattered Israel returning to the Lord and receiving revelation.

This chapter contains 2 verses and records the Lord instructing David W. Patten to settle his business and dispose of merchandise so he can go on a mission next spring with eleven others to testify worldwide. It also states that those who deny the Lord’s name will be replaced, and others will be appointed in their stead to receive their bishopric.

This chapter contains 19 verses and records a revelation to Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, Hyrum Smith, Edward Partridge, and Church leaders, naming the Church “The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.” It calls members to gather to Zion and its stakes for defense and refuge. Far West is declared holy, and a temple is commanded with specific start dates, diligence, and a revealed pattern, avoiding debt. It directs Far West’s rapid building and appointing other stakes, affirming Joseph’s keys.

This chapter contains 1 verse and records the Lord naming Spring Hill “Adam-ondi-Ahman,” stating it is the place where Adam will visit his people and where the Ancient of Days will sit, as spoken of by Daniel the prophet.

This chapter contains 16 verses and records instructions to William Marks and Newel K. Whitney to settle Kirtland business, repay debts, repent of covetousness, and depart before winter to Zion. It assigns Marks to preside at Far West and Whitney to serve as bishop at Adam-ondi-Ahman. It addresses Oliver Granger to seek redemption of the First Presidency’s obligations and come to Zion. It tells Kirtland servants to preserve the Lord’s house and overthrow moneychangers.

This chapter contains 6 verses and records the Lord directing an immediate conference, organizing the Twelve, and appointing replacements for fallen members. Thomas is to remain in Zion to publish the word. The others are to continue preaching with humility, with a promise of provision for their families and an opened door. Next spring they depart over the great waters, leaving Far West April 26. John Taylor, John E. Page, Wilford Woodruff, and Willard Richards are appointed.

This chapter contains 7 verses and records the Lord requiring surplus property be given to the bishop in Zion for building the Lord’s house, establishing Zion, supporting the priesthood, and paying Presidency debts. It institutes tithing: after the initial surplus, members pay one-tenth of their interest annually as a standing law. Those gathering to Zion must obey or are unworthy to abide; keeping the law sanctifies Zion, and it applies to all stakes.

This chapter contains 1 verse and records the Lord directing that certain matters be disposed of by a council composed of the First Presidency, the bishop and his council, and the high council, with decisions guided by the Lord’s voice to them.

This chapter contains 46 verses and records a plea to God regarding persecutions, followed by comfort that adversity is temporary and endurance brings exaltation. It pronounces woes and judgments on those who falsely accuse, oppress, and murder the Saints, including loss of priesthood rights. It promises revealed knowledge in the dispensation of the fulness of times and teaches that priesthood power operates only through righteousness, persuasion, meekness, charity, and without compulsion.

This chapter contains 9 verses and records assurances to an afflicted servant that enemies will mock and persecute him, but the pure in heart will seek counsel and blessings from him and traitors will not turn his people against him. It lists possible tribulations, imprisonment, separation from family, and threats of death, stating these give experience and work for good. It notes the Son of Man descends below all and commands him to continue, promising priesthood, limits on adversaries, and God’s continual support.

This chapter contains 17 verses and records an instruction for the Saints to gather and document facts about their sufferings in the state, including property losses, injuries, and names of oppressors. It directs appointing a committee to collect statements, affidavits, and libelous publications, and to present these to the world and government leaders. It urges earnest, persistent effort, not treating these matters as small, and encourages doing all within their power.

This chapter contains 145 verses and records a revelation to Joseph Smith commanding a solemn proclamation to world rulers and directing construction of the Nauvoo Temple and the Nauvoo House. It sets requirements and deadlines for baptisms for the dead and other ordinances to be performed in a dedicated house. It names and assigns duties to leaders, organizes quorums and councils, establishes stock and governance rules for the Nauvoo House, gives counsel to specific individuals, and instructs the Church to fill offices and prepare rooms in the temple.

This chapter contains 4 verses and records the Lord’s will for saints in the Territory of Iowa to keep commandments, gather to appointed places designated through Joseph, and build cities in the Lord’s name. It directs building a city opposite Nauvoo named Zarahemla. It also instructs migrants from all directions to take inheritances in Zarahemla, Nashville, Nauvoo, and other appointed stakes.

This chapter contains 3 verses and records the Lord’s message to Brigham Young that he is no longer required to leave his family as before, because his past offering is acceptable. It acknowledges his labor and journeyings for the Lord’s name and commands him to send the word abroad while taking especial care of his family from then on.

This chapter contains 12 verses and records Joseph Smith’s letter about leaving temporarily for safety due to legal pursuit, while agents manage his debts and affairs. It commands Saints to continue temple work with diligence amid persecution. It gives instructions on baptism for the dead, requiring an eyewitness recorder and orderly records for temple archives, linking earthly records with heavenly binding and loosing.

This chapter contains 25 verses and records instructions on baptism for the dead and the required record-keeping: ward recorders and a general church recorder document ordinances with dates, names, and witnesses. It links earthly records with heavenly records and cites Revelation 20, Matthew 16, 1 Corinthians 15, and Malachi 4. It references angelic restorations (Moroni, Michael, Peter, James, John) and urges preparing a temple book of the dead’s records.

This chapter contains 9 verses and records teachings about two kinds of heavenly beings: resurrected angels with bodies of flesh and bones, and spirits of just men made perfect who are not resurrected. It gives instructions for testing a messenger claiming a message from God by offering a handshake to discern an angel, a just spirit, or the devil appearing as an angel of light, and identifies these as keys to recognize administrations from God.

This chapter contains 23 verses and records teachings about seeing the Savior as a man, continued sociality after this life, and a personal appearing of the Father and Son. It addresses differing reckoning of time by planets, angels ministering only to their own earth, and God’s residence as a Urim and Thummim; the sanctified earth and individual white stones function similarly. It includes prophecy of bloodshed beginning in South Carolina, a statement about Joseph Smith possibly seeing the Son of Man, principles of intelligence gained in mortality, blessings tied to obedience to law, and the embodied nature of the Father and Son versus the Holy Ghost.

This chapter contains 8 verses and records teachings on celestial glory having three degrees and that the highest requires entering the new and everlasting covenant of marriage; without it one cannot obtain the highest and cannot have increase. It defines the “more sure word of prophecy” as knowing by revelation through priesthood power that one is sealed to eternal life. It states salvation is impossible in ignorance and teaches that spirit is refined matter discernible when bodies are purified.

This chapter contains 66 verses and records a revelation to Joseph Smith about the new and everlasting covenant, including eternal marriage sealed by priesthood authority and the Holy Spirit of promise. It explains consequences for rejecting the covenant, contrasts sealed versus unsealed marriages, and defines adultery and related judgments. It cites Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, David, and Solomon regarding plural wives by commandment. It grants sealing and remitting powers to Joseph, addresses Emma Smith with specific commands, and outlines conditions for taking additional wives with consent.

This chapter contains 74 verses and records the Lord’s call for church members to sanctify themselves, leave Babylon, hold solemn assemblies, and gather to Zion, with Judah to Jerusalem. It commands elders to preach the everlasting gospel to all nations. It describes the Lord’s coming to his temple and reign, earth changes, Israel’s gathering (including Ephraim and north countries), resurrection of saints, judgment on the wicked, and promises of eternal life to the repentant.

This chapter contains 12 verses and covers statements on government and law, requiring protection of conscience, property, and life; the role of magistrates; limits on civil control of religion; citizens sustaining lawful governments while rejecting sedition; equal protection for religious belief; punishment of crimes; separation of religious influence from civil government; church discipline limited to fellowship and excommunication; seeking civil redress and self-defense in emergencies; and preaching the gospel without interfering with bond-servants against masters’ will.

This chapter contains 7 verses and records the deaths of Joseph Smith and Hyrum Smith, killed by an armed mob at Carthage Jail on June 27, 1844. It notes John Taylor is wounded and Willard Richards unharmed. It recounts Joseph’s statements before surrendering at Carthage and Hyrum reading from Ether 12. It gives their ages, asserts their innocence, and identifies their martyrdom as sealing their testimony and the books’ publication.

This chapter contains 42 verses and records instructions for organizing the Camp of Israel into companies with captains and presidencies under the Twelve, providing wagons and supplies, sending pioneers, and caring for the poor and families left behind. It names leaders to organize companies, commands unity, honesty, sobriety, and stewardship, and gives promises and warnings about trials, Zion’s redemption, enemies, and keeping commandments.

This chapter contains 10 verses and records a vision of the celestial kingdom, including its gate, streets, and the throne where the Father and the Son sit. Joseph sees Adam, Abraham, his parents, and his brother Alvin, and wonders about Alvin’s inheritance. The Lord states that those who die without knowledge of the gospel but would have received it, and children who die before accountability, inherit the celestial kingdom, and that judgment is by works and desires.

This chapter contains 60 verses and records Joseph F. Smith’s 1918 vision of the spirit world while pondering 1 Peter. He sees righteous spirits assembled awaiting Christ, who preaches resurrection and redemption to them. Christ does not visit the wicked but commissions righteous messengers to preach repentance, faith, and vicarious ordinances to spirits in darkness. Adam, Eve, Abel, Noah, Abraham, Moses, prophets, Nephite prophets, and latter-day leaders are present; temple work and continued missionary labor among the dead are described.
